title: Control of small-flowered nutsedge in rice crop fields - Vietnam

Header: Control of small-flowered nutsedge in rice crop fields - Vietnam
Cyperus difformis Cỏtò ty, cỏcháo, cỏlác dù

Prevention: Prevention is particularly important as the weed is difficult to control.
Seeds are the main means of spread.
Clean tools and farm machinery after working in an infested area to prevent spread.
Flooding of rice fields to a depth of 5-10cm for 10-15 days strongly suppresses the growth of
Rotate crop every season or annually, as applicable, with non- flooded crop such as maize, soybean, and vegetables.
Monitoring: Erect, perennial sedge, up to 80cm high, with smooth, triangular, slightly winged stems; numerous reddish fibrous roots; 3-4 basal leaves, smooth, flat and linear up to 25cm long; tubular sheaths, united at base, often without leaf blades at the base; inflorescence consists of several dense, umbrella-like heads, 2-6cm long, emerging from the tip of the stem, each topped by 3-8 purplish- brown flowerheads.
Fruits are brownish elliptical nuts, about 0.6mm long and lightly pitted.
Monitor fields weekly in the first 30 days after transplanting/sowing and consider direct control if weed is present.
Direct Control: Hand weeding, raking and hoeing in row- planted rice plants can provide effective control.

Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
